## Content-SLO decision and research brief

- Last qualifying publication **October 27, 10:06:46 PDT**; exact 48-hour deadline **October 29, 10:06:46 PDT**. Waiting for the next approximately 09:00 PDT cycle would breach the deadline. Today prioritizes an independently supported technical publication.
- Reader question: why an AgentSight TLS/HTTP response still looks compressed or has no decoded model text, and what evidence distinguishes capture truncation from decoding failure.
- Decision/evidence: synthetic unit-test and source-level analysis of `HTTPDecompressor`, backed by product commit `c1574366...`, `collector/src/cmd_trace.rs`, `ext/analysis/src/analyzers/http_decompressor.rs`, `http_parser.rs`, `sse_processor.rs` and `docs/ssl-capture.md`. Original ten-case table contrasts codecs, byte fidelity, chunk framing, missing bytes, non-response events and stacked encodings. Includes a reproducible pinned-source `cargo test --manifest-path ext/analysis/Cargo.toml http_decompressor::tests` procedure, clearly marked not executed.
- Semantic-overlap decision: `/blog/how-agentsight-correlates-http-exchanges/` owns request/response identity, stream matching and capture loss; it does not document gzip/Brotli/Zstd codec matrix, rewritten decoded fields or test-level decoder behavior. The new canonical `/blog/why-agentsight-compressed-http-responses-stay-encoded/` owns **response decoding fidelity**. Cross-link rather than duplicate the HTTP correlation answer.
- Narrow rendered scope: new standalone TechArticle route, Blog card/CollectionPage entry and sitemap registration. No template/design/analytics/routing migration. Acceptance: live canonical page visibly answers decoding question with one H1, source links and table; Blog links it and sitemap includes it exactly once. Representative unchanged `/`, `/blog/how-agentsight-correlates-http-exchanges/`, `/product/`. Rollback baseline `c9b4bc46...`.
- Release claims and metadata pinned to v1.0.35. No invented end-to-end capture measurements or customer data.
